newsitem.title: USA: U.S. holds Milosevic responsible for violence.
newsitem.headline: U.S. holds Milosevic responsible for violence.

text.p: The United States said on Tuesday it held Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic responsible for the violent actions of loyalist demonstrators who fought fierce battles with rival opposition protesters.

"The U.S. holds the Serbian government and its president, Slobodan Milosevic, responsible for the violent actions of the demonstrators," acting Secretary of State Strobe Talbott said in a prepared statement.
Talbott said the top U.S. diplomat in Belgrade, Richard Miles, had met Serbian Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic on Tuesday to urge the Serbian government to avoid further violence.
"We have given a similar message to the opposition," he said after a day of street of battles in which a man was shot in the head.

About 40,000 Milosevic supporters, a fraction of those expected, turned out on Tuesday for a pro-government rally, a blow to Milosevic's attempts to quell 35 days of protests by opposition parties who accused him of election fraud after he voided their victories in November 17 local elections.

Talbott placed the responsiblity for the flareup on the government. "Rather than making a goodwill effort to resolve the political crisis caused by the annulment of oppostion victories in the November 17 elections, the Serbian authorities have flagrantly and provocatively chosen to heighten tensions by bringing thousands of people into Belgrade to confront the peaceful demonstrations by the opposition," he said.
